'''William Munger Boothby''' (April 1, 1918 – February 14, 2021) was an American mathematician and professor emeritus of mathematics at [[Arts and Sciences at Washington University in St. Louis]],<ref name="obit">{{citation|url=https://source.wustl.edu/2021/04/obituary-william-m-boothby-professor-emeritus-of-mathematics-102/|title=Obituary: William M. Boothby, professor emeritus of mathematics, 102|work=|publisher=[[Washington University in St. Louis]]|date=April 29, 2021}}</ref> known for his work in [[differential geometry]] including the book ''An introduction to differentiable manifolds and Riemannian geometry'' (1975; 2nd ed. 1986).<ref name=":0">Reviews of ''An introduction to differentiable manifolds and Riemannian geometry'': R. J. Crittenden, {{MR|0426007}}; P. Wintgen, {{zbl|0333.53001}}; K.Chandrasekhara Rao, {{zbl|0596.53001}}; Robert Szczarba, ''American Scientist'', {{JSTOR|27855267}}; T. J. Willmore, ''Bull. London Math. Soc.'', {{doi|10.1112/blms/19.5.489}}</ref>

== Education and career ==
Boothby was originally from [[Detroit]]. He received a six-year scholarship to attend the [[Cranbrook Academy of Art|Cranbrook Academy]] in [[Bloomfield Hills, Michigan|Bloomfield Hills]], and completed a degree at the [[University of Michigan]] in 1940. His graduate studies in mathematics were interrupted by [[World War II]]; he became a pilot for the [[United States Army Air Forces]] between 1942 and 1945.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last= |date=2021-04-21 |title=Remembering Dr. William Boothby |url=https://math.washu.edu/news/remembering-dr-william-boothby |access-date=2026-08-21 |website=[[Washington University in St. Louis]] |language=en}}</ref>

He would complete a PhD at University of Michigan in 1949.<ref name="obit" /> His dissertation, ''A Topological Study of the Level Curves of Harmonic Functions'', was supervised by [[Wilfred Kaplan]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy |id=5158}}</ref>

He then joined as junior faculty [[Northwestern University]]. A one-year fellowship at [[ETH Zurich]] followed in 1950-51. He joined as a professor the Mathematics Department at the [[Washington University in St. Louis]], until his retirement in 1988. In 1960-61 he visited the [[Institute for Advanced Study]].<ref name="obit" /><ref name=":1" />

== Research ==
His early research concerned [[differential geometry]], including [[Harmonic function|harmonic functions]], [[Hermitian manifold|Hermitian manifolds]] and [[Contact geometry|contact structures]]. In particular, he worked on contact manifolds together with [[Hsien Chung Wang]], describing what is now known as the [[Boothby-Wang construction]].<ref name=":1" /> 

In 1975 he published a very popular textbook, ''An Introduction to Differentiable Manifolds and Riemannian Geometry'', which "defined the curriculum and standard of the introductory graduate differential geometry course worldwide".<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" />

After publishing this book, his research interests shifted to [[control theory]].<ref name="obit" /><ref name=":1" />
